skill.name: brenda-database
skill.description: Access the BRENDA enzyme database through SOAP API examples and helper scripts. Retrieve kinetic parameters, reactions, organism comparisons, substrate specificity, and pathway analysis inputs.
skill.summary: Query BRENDA enzyme records for kinetics, reactions, organism comparisons, and pathway analysis.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts were false positives from EC numbers, Markdown code fences, normal imports, and public documentation URLs. Confirmed issues are limited to BRENDA credential handling through .env guidance and local export or report writes to caller-supplied filenames. No prompt-injection text or hidden malicious intent was found in the scanned files.

remediation.issue: BRENDA credentials are stored through .env guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend environment variables or a secrets manager, warn users not to commit .env, and avoid printing credential values.

remediation.issue: The documented environment loader can read credential files.
remediation.suggestion: Limit loaded keys to BRENDA_EMAIL and BRENDA_PASSWORD, validate file permissions, and avoid arbitrary .env paths.

remediation.issue: Export and report functions write to caller-supplied filenames.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict default writes to an output directory, normalize paths, and warn before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: The skill sends authenticated requests to an external BRENDA service.
remediation.suggestion: Clearly disclose that credentials are used only for BRENDA API calls and keep rate limiting enabled.

static_findings.snippet: - `Invalid parameters`: Check parameter format and order
- Verify account is active and has API access
print("\n2. Comparing alcohol dehydrogenase (1.1.1.1) across organisms:")
print(f"No valid data for organism comparison of EC {ec_number}")
- Note: There's also `BRENDA_EMIAL` (note the typo) for legacy support
- `get_modeling_parameters(ec_number, substrate)`: Get parameters for kinetic modeling
- `export_kinetic_data(ec_number, format, filename)`: Export data to file
- Verify BRENDA_EMAIL and BRENDA_PASSWORD in .env file

content.value_statement: Biochemistry teams need reliable enzyme data for kinetics, reactions, and pathway design. This skill provides BRENDA query, parsing, export, and visualization workflows.
actual_capabilities: Queries BRENDA for Km values, reaction equations, organisms, inhibitors, activators, and cofactors.
Parses BRENDA response strings into structured enzyme, substrate, organism, pH, and temperature fields.
Compares enzyme properties across organisms and supports substrate or product-based enzyme search.
Exports kinetic data as CSV, JSON, or Excel files for downstream analysis.
Generates plots for kinetic parameters, pH profiles, temperature profiles, and Michaelis-Menten curves.
Builds basic retrosynthetic pathway reports from BRENDA-derived enzyme candidates.
limitations: Requires a valid BRENDA account and local credentials.
Depends on external BRENDA availability, response format, and rate limits.
Helper scripts require optional Python packages such as zeep, pandas, matplotlib, seaborn, and networkx.
Pathway suggestions are heuristic and need scientific validation before laboratory use.

use_cases.title: Screen Enzyme Candidates
use_cases.description: Find enzymes that use a substrate or produce a target molecule, then compare kinetic evidence.

use_cases.title: Compare Organism Variants
use_cases.description: Review enzyme data across organisms to identify candidates with useful temperature, pH, or cofactor properties.

use_cases.title: Prepare Pathway Reports
use_cases.description: Build preliminary retrosynthesis notes and export BRENDA-derived evidence for design review.

prompt_templates.title: Find Kinetic Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Km values for EC 1.1.1.1 in BRENDA and summarize the organisms, substrates, and reported conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Organisms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare alcohol dehydrogenase EC 1.1.1.1 across Escherichia coli, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and Homo sapiens. Highlight kinetic and condition differences.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Engineering Targets
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify thermophilic or alkaline-stable variants for EC 1.1.1.1 and list evidence that supports each candidate.

prompt_templates.title: Build Pathway Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use BRENDA-derived evidence to propose an enzymatic pathway to lactate. Include enzyme candidates, missing data, feasibility notes, and export options.

output_examples.input: Find Km data for alcohol dehydrogenase.
output_examples.output: A short report listing organisms, substrates, Km ranges, experimental conditions, and caveats about missing units or inconsistent records.

output_examples.input: Compare enzyme variants for heat tolerance.
output: Candidate organism summary with reported optimal temperatures.
Kinetic evidence that supports each candidate.
Limitations where BRENDA lacks complete pH or temperature data.

output_examples.input: Prepare a pathway report for lactate.
output_examples.output: A pathway feasibility note with candidate EC numbers, organism options, substrate-product steps, and recommended validation checks.

best_practices: Use specific EC numbers, organisms, and substrates to reduce broad BRENDA queries.
Keep BRENDA credentials in local environment variables and do not include them in prompts or shared files.
Validate all kinetic values against primary literature before experimental decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat pathway reports as laboratory-ready protocols.
Do not run broad wildcard searches without rate limiting.
Do not publish exported files that contain private project context or account details.

faq.question: Does this skill require BRENDA credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. BRENDA API access requires an account email and password stored locally or set as environment variables.

faq.question: Can it create visualizations?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper scripts can generate plots for kinetics, pH, temperature, organism comparison, and Michaelis-Menten curves.

faq.question: Does it include the BRENDA database locally?
faq.answer: No. It queries the external BRENDA service and depends on that service being available.

faq.question: Can it export data?
faq.answer: Yes. It can export parsed kinetic data to CSV, JSON, or Excel files.

faq.question: Are pathway suggestions experimentally validated?
faq.answer: No. They are evidence summaries and heuristics that require expert review and literature validation.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
